note: The Handover mission layer, moved out of the world: destinations and crew (block frame, from the old handover-block.json, suborned.block/2), the plan routes (getaway, official), and the rules that read them (C-3 mission points land on a plot or street, M-1 routes reach their end, W-1 walk origins from standards.walking.from). The world holds none of it. Input to brief 003. Run: bun tools/plan/cli.ts --overlay tools/missions/handover/overlay.ts. suborned.mission/2 (2026-10-14) adds the schedule the world's life rules held until Pulse regenerated them: status, clock, timeline, events, stands. Re-sited 2026-10-14 (Waymark; brief 008 B2, Vantage): the Records Office doors now stand on its tower faces, so four door points follow them. Office entrance (54.65, -30.5) to (51.75, -30), on the public landing 0.75 m up six steps; Office approach (52, -30.5) to (48.6, -30), at the foot of those steps; Official entrance and Meet Vale (73.25, -31) to (76.25, -30), the flush official door under the canopy. 'Steps' is renamed 'Terrace gate' (the café door is flush, there are no steps; the point has not moved). The door points equal the civic block's entrances: tools/missions/handover/moves.test.ts. Nothing else is re-sited and nothing is re-timed: every schedule entry is a clock offset from GDD §07 and names no leg and no walking pace, so none follows from a length that changed. Every time is a mission-clock offset; GDD §07 is the authority for the timeline. The removed originals, verbatim: git show 15af5dd:contracts/world/harbour-district.life.json (clock.mission, clock.anchors, events.list[0], traffic.rules[3], generator.civicEmployers[0].shiftEnd, transit.schedule). suborned.mission/3 (2026-10-15, Waymark; brief 010 D) adds roles: the people the mission needs by role (employer, position or role, mission point, shift window), never by person; the overlay casts each from the generated people and pins one by id (rule M-2). The cell's start re-sited 2026-10-16 (Waymark; brief 014, Sky playing the Handover: "you can't see them! That's a very bad start"): the four stood in a 1.2 m line at (1.168..4.768, -49.666), on the kerb strip of Rocket Lane, where bld/rocket-west/19 stands between them and the play camera (V-1: 6 % of a figure seen). They now stand loosely by the getaway car, as people waiting at the square's boarding pavilion would, inside the keep-clear zone the block keeps for them (crew-line-getaway): Fixer (-0.2, -46.6), Tech (1.2, -44.6), Scout (-1.6, -44.3), Enforcer (2.7, -47.6), 2.4-3.4 m from each neighbour. Each is 100 % seen at the play camera (zoom 14, 38 degrees, yaw 30), out from under the pavilion's canopy, on a free cell of the engine's walk grid, 23 m or more from every watcher's fan at 0:00 and 5.9 m or more from any person's place (P-16). GDD section 07's 'cell at getaway car' still holds; the Enforcer stands nearest the car. Walks (tools/plan/walk-fine.ts): Scout to beside Inez 25.0 to 18.6 m, Fixer to the cafe door 26.4 to 23.2 m, Tech to the cabinet 39.6 to 36.0 m, Enforcer to the Office approach 49.3 to 50.9 m. The opening view centres on block (-2.5, -40.5): briefs/014/waymark-start.png. Schema: contracts/missions/mission.schema.ts. Test: tools/missions/handover/mission.test.ts.

clock.src: Sky's ruling 2026-10-15 (clock.ruling): the 5:30 handover chime is the Records Office's real shift end, life.generator.civicEmployers[0].shiftEnd 17:30, so 0:00 = 17:30 less 5:30. GDD §07 gives offsets only, no day time. The 8-12 min mission window stays a world rule (life.clock.mission.windowMin, GDD §01).
clock.transit: 17:24:30 = 62670 s, 30 s past a multiple of 120, 180 and 240 (62640 s). With phase 0 and the peak headways (S1 120 s, T1 180 s, T2 240 s) every line left its first stop 30 s before mission 0:00; the next forward departures are 1:30 (S1), 2:30 (T1) and 3:30 (T2). Under the old 17:00 start every line left at 0:00 (removed life.transit.schedule: '17:00 = 61200 s is a multiple of 120, 180 and 240').

rivals.src: Sky 2026-10-16 (via Aster: 'a rival gang that has menace level authority is a +1'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md, a public fight, rule 4: the Handover's rivals are menace
rivals.note: How the public sees this mission's rival crew: menace (feared) or neutral (not). The rulebook's fight.public reads it: breaking feared rivals in a public fight is +1 Standing, firing first on rivals nobody fears is -1; without it the rulebook's fight.rivalsPublic (menace) stands. Adopted by Waymark 2026-10-16 as Keel wrote it, kept a top-level block rather than a field on a role: the rivals are a crew the mission sends, not people cast from the district (roles names only cast people), so they have no role to carry it. Menace because the Handover's rivals come to take a councillor off the street outside the Records Office, and a crew that takes people off the street is feared (motive-standing rule 4). tools/sim/site.ts reads it into the site (rivals.public); tools/missions/handover/mission.test.ts locks it.
